name: Autosomal Recessive Primary Immunodeficiency with Defective Spontaneous Natural Killer Cell Cytotoxicity
aliases: AR Primary Immunodeficiency with NK Cell Dysfunction
NK Cell Cytotoxicity Deficiency, Autosomal Recessive

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: NK Cell Cytotoxicity Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Demonstrated defective spontaneous natural killer (NK) cell cytotoxicity in functional assays
Recurrent severe viral infections, particularly herpesviruses
Identification of biallelic pathogenic variants in genes associated with NK cell cytotoxicity defects
Normal or reduced NK cell counts with impaired cytotoxic function

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of defective spontaneous NK cell cytotoxicity plus recurrent severe viral infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical and functional criteria are met.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Defective spontaneous natural killer cell cytotoxicity
pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by functional NK cell assays
Including herpes simplex virus and varicella zoster virus

common.notes: Frequent upper and lower respiratory tract infections
Persistent fungal infections of skin and mucosa
searchTerms: chronic yeast infections on skin and mucous

common.notes: Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic infections
Poor growth related to chronic illness
searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

occasional.notes: Enlargement of liver and spleen due to immune activation
Due to infections or immune dysregulation

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to viral encephalitis

rare.notes: Non-healing ulcers due to immune dysfunction

laboratory: Reduced or absent NK cell cytotoxic activity on chromium release or flow cytometry-based assays
Normal or decreased NK cell counts by immunophenotyping
Elevated serum viral loads during infections
imaging: Lymphadenopathy and hepatosplenomegaly on ultrasound or CT scans
Possible CNS imaging abnormalities in viral encephalitis
other: Histopathology showing hemophagocytosis in bone marrow during HLH episodes

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of mutations in PRF1, UNC13D, STX11 genes
Severe HLH episodes with impaired cytotoxicity of both NK and CD8+ T cells

redFlags: Severe recurrent herpesvirus infections in infancy or early childhood
Markedly reduced NK cell cytotoxicity despite normal NK cell numbers
references: Orange JS. Natural killer cell deficiency. J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2013;132(3):515-525.
Mace EM, Orange JS. Genetic causes of human NK cell deficiency and their effect on NK cell subsets. Front Immunol. 2019;10:181.

Al-Herz W, et al. Primary immunodeficiency diseases: an update on the classification from the International Union of Immunological Societies Expert Committee for Primary Immunodeficiency 2019. J Clin Immunol. 2020;40(1):24-64.
